title: Supply-Side Equilibria in Recommender Systems
authors: Meena Jagadeesan, Nikhil Garg, and Jacob Steinhardt
main_caveat: Finite Section 2 primitives, Proposition pure finite-deviation routes, a conditional Proposition atom product-integral route, single-genre CDF/optimization algebra, two-user induced-cost and regionscolor calculus plus the supportrestriction content-to-value-ball/canonical-feasible-domain/C1-ball/local-max/FOC/cross-partial, polar-chart, and bracket-nonvanishing substeps, literal Ptwo and finiteP standard-basis C1 maximizer steps (the finiteP route uses coordinate bounds rather than the source's false unit-radius assertion), infinite-genre algebra, support-cap pieces of Proposition existence, and exact Ptwo and finiteP source constructions are formalized. The Ptwo angle sampler equals the stated zero-extended density measure, the circle measure has exact literal-circle topological support and direct P=2 C2 marginals, and a concrete almost-everywhere-nonnegative Content 2 measure transports through the actual standard-basis score map to that circle law. Its fixed score levels are null, so the actual uniform-tie assigned-user mass against every pure action is the source sum of marginal CDF values. On the actual nonnegative source action domain, the corresponding cost-subtracted payoff is bounded by `1 - 2 / beta`, with equality for support actions at either producer index; those support actions are direct best responses over nonnegative deviations. The finiteP unit-interval source-curve sampler gives a nonnegative content probability law whose standard-basis score law is exactly its coordinate law. Its coordinate and transported standard-basis value laws have the literal curve as exact topological support, and both coordinate CDFs satisfy the proposition's zero-extended `min(1, z^(2/(P-1)))` law and the equivalent direct C2 root-CDF equality. This closes the direct finiteP C1/C2/C3 components, but not the generic necessary/sufficient or mixed-Nash semantic bridge. The structural source statements' explicit absolutely continuous score-law hypothesis now has a checked tie-null and weak-CDF payoff consequence. The canonical two-user transport separately turns a visible topological content-support l2 ball into a realized-value support ball; under nonzero sine and a.e. nonnegative content, its actual value-map image is a closed feasible domain containing that ball. The C1-ball endpoint now derives its nonzero polar point and angle interval internally. None derives the map/law identification, either support ball, nonzero sine, a.e. content nonnegativity, a source-valid generic C1 domain, pointwise derivatives, or a valid generic C1-C3 theorem from equilibrium semantics. The proof prose at `arxiv-update.tex:1706` conflicts with the proposition's CDF except at `P = 3`. The Ptwo facts remain intentionally unbundled. The full paper remains open; the main boundaries are general mixed-measure semantics and existence, a source-faithful tie-aware necessary/sufficient bridge, the source-to-supportrestriction canonical-map/feasible-domain/C1 bridge, and later distributional work for the continuous-equilibrium results.
human_summary: Formalization gap: Theorem 2 uses a specific two-dimensional user model; Theorems 3–4 cover user vectors at angles below 90°; Lemma 2 proves a restricted equilibrium characterization.

llm_statement_review.policy: For every selected source claim, compare only its exact byte-pinned raw source-anchor bundle and Lean's expanded transparent `...Spec : Prop` target. The paired proof endpoint receives separate Lean-Meta proof credit; a name, paraphrase, wrapper, or prior aggregate receipt is not a semantic match. Review every retained paper-local prerequisite and every material library prerequisite before the dependent claim.

llm_paper_coverage_review.policy: Maintain a source inventory before closeout, then check source-to-interface coverage separately from row-local statement matching.

llm_assumption_review.policy: Any paper-facing theorem premise not derived from prior Lean declarations must be routed through Assumptions.lean and judged against the source.

llm_source_record_review.policy: Run only if the paper-facing interface uses records, certificates, replay objects, or broad source-row packages.

source_proof_fidelity_review.policy: Audit source proof steps and source-model defects by exact source locator and mathematical claim, not Lean declaration names. Ledger schema 2 records all literal source-statement defects and their corrected source targets. Every approved corrected target must name its governing defect and expose every added regularity at its source-facing Spec; neither a defect record nor maintainer authorization supplies proof credit.
